scope: Theorem 3.4 (Peanosphere realization) of the manuscript “Canonical conformal limits of subcritical FK planar maps” (preprints/Canonical-conformal-limits-of-subcritical-FK-planar-maps-September-24-2026/main.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 211 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 e7dab39caf778176), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 12. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: The bilateral Brownian contour is the boundary-length process of a γ-quantum cone explored by an independent, unparameterized whole-plane space-filling SLEκ, subsequently parameterized by quantum area. The duration-one excursion is the boundary- length process of the ordinary unit-area γ-quantum sphere explored in the same way from an area-typical marked point p∗. The contour determines the curve-decorated quantum surface up to its marked conformal equivalence. Write η for the exploration parameterized by quantum area. In either realization, η∗(dt) = µh. Its spatial identifications are generated by finite chains of scalar horizontal chords s ∼L t ⇐⇒ Ls = Lt = inf [s,t] L, s < t, (3.2) and the analogous R-chords, with the usual endpoint identification for the sphere. The resulting quotient carries the topology of the plane, or sphere, respectively. Frontier arcs are parameterized by quantum length, with running-minimum contour heights as their length coordinates.
